additionalCoursework:
- We strongly recommend that applicants take as many upper-level human-based Biology courses as they are able. Course types include, but are not limited to, Cell Biology, Genetics, Anatomy and Physiology, Microbiology, and Immunology.

Semester versus Quarter Hours:
- UNM School of Medicine Requires that applicants take either two semesters or three quarters of the required prerequisite coursework. 
- It is the applicant's responsibility to ensure they meet our prerequisite course work and credit hour requirements which may differ from their institutional graduation requirements. 
- Please utilize the AMCAS Application Grade Conversion Guide to determine how your quarter credits will be converted to semester credits: https://students-residents.aamc.org/media/7761/download

medSchoolStudLife.diversity: The UNM Health Sciences Center’s most important value is a steadfast duty to improve the health of all New Mexicans. We will serve our patients and the public with integrity and accountability. We will strive as an institution and as individuals to recognize, cultivate and promote all forms of diversity; to fully understand the health needs of our communities; and to advance clinical, academic, and research excellence. We are committed to perform our duties with compassion and respect for our patients, learners, and colleagues; and always to conduct ourselves with the highest level of professionalism.
medSchoolStudLife.leaveOfAbsence: Students may request a Leave of Absence (LOA) from the curriculum for personal or academic reasons. The student must complete the leave of absence request form and submit to the Office of Medical Student Affairs. The Associate Dean of Students reviews all requests and may forward to the Committee for Student Promotion and Evaluation for final approval. Emergency LOAs may be granted for personal or family emergencies.
medSchoolStudLife.organizationActivities: The University of New Mexico School of Medicine student organizations are centered on different areas of student life: cultural, religious, social, academic, professional, and community service. The Office of Medical Student Affairs is cognizant of the benefits of active student involvement and offers support for over 40 student organizations. Medical students are involved in projects, organizations and activities that extend beyond the classroom and into the community.
medSchoolStudLife.setting: Nestled between the towering Sandia Mountains and the Rio Grande Valley, the School of Medicine is located in the heart of Albuquerque and next door to the UNM Hospital and New Mexico's only Level One Trauma Center. Enjoy 310 days of sunshine along with a mild, dry climate and four distinctly beautiful seasons. Very low humidity means that even when temperatures rise, summer is always comfortable, and our sunny winters are comparatively mild.
medSchoolStudLife.housing: On-campus housing is not available. However, the School of Medicine is located near the historic Nob Hill neighborhood where students will find many affordable rental prospects. UNM offers courtyard-style graduate and family housing south of main campus. Also available is the brand new student housing community, Lobo Village, conveniently located with unmatched amenities.
medSchoolStudLife.supportSystems: Lesbian, gay, bisexual, transgender, intersex and queer people face unique physical and mental health challenges. New Mexico needs compassionate LGBTQ+ health care providers and allies like you to provide the safe, effective, respectful care all patients deserve. We are dedicated to recognizing and stopping discrimination, eliminating health care inequities and respectfully advocating for our LGBTQ+ patients, students, trainees and colleagues.
medSchoolStudLife.supportSystemsForDisabilities:
Disability-related accommodations requests are reviewed individually, on a case-by-case basis, to determine whether there are any reasonable accommodations or available options that would permit the candidate to satisfy the Technical Standards for Admissions.

Students requiring accommodations should contact the liaison to the Accessibility Resource Center (ARC) to request accommodations: https://arc.unm.edu/about-us/contact-us.html. ARC will engage in a conﬁdential, collaborative, and interactive process with the student and UNM SOM leadership to determine reasonable accommodations. Given the clinical nature of medical education, additional time may be needed to implement accommodations. Timely disclosure and requests by students are essential and encouraged as accommodations are not applied retroactively. The UNM SOM reserves the right to request new or additional information in support of requests.
medSchoolStudLife.wellnessPrograms: The commitment of the Office of Medical Student Wellness to supporting students' well-being through workshops, resiliency programs, and incorporating self-care into the curriculum is crucial. Addressing the wellness of medical students is vital for their overall success and mental health. Integrating these elements into the curriculum not only acknowledges the challenges of medical education but also provides practical tools and strategies for students to prioritize their well-being.
medSchoolStudLife.campusCulture: The UNM HSC culture transcends "tolerance." We live, breathe and reach for new perspectives that help us grow together as individuals and providers in our great state. At the heart of it all is a steady pulse of boundless welcoming, respect and honor for all New Mexicans. Our mission is rooted in continual learning and enhancing the experiences of LGBTQ+, first generation, BIPOC and women's experiences at UNM HSC and the health system. We attract expert faculty with a passion for serving those most in need. And our graduates, residents and fellows gain exemplary patient care, research and collegial experience.
medSchoolStudLife.transportationAdditionalInfo: There are no transportation requirements for medical students. You may visit https://pats.unm.edu/ if you have any questions.

medSchoolCurriculum.tutoringPrograms: Faculty hold weekly office hours; peer to peer tutors work with more junior students; and learning specialists assist with learning and test-taking strategies.
medSchoolCurriculum.instructionStyle: Active and interactive learning-based curriculum. Experiential activities in clinical settings start the second half of Year 1. Experiential learning is the main type of instruction in Years 3 & 4.
medSchoolCurriculum.clinicalRotations: Family Practice, Internal Medicine, Neurology, Obstetrics and Gynecology, Pediatrics, Psychiatry, and Surgery
medSchoolCurriculum.prematriculationProgram: Please see the "Special Programs" section to learn more about our Premedical Enrichment Program (PrEP).
medSchoolCurriculum.lectureAttendance: No required lecture attendance, although attendance at some active learning is required
medSchoolCurriculum.curricularHighlights: The School of Medicine integrates basic sciences and clinical medicine with student-centered and active-learning techniques.  Early clinical skills including physical exam training and patient-centered communication are emphasized as early as the first semester. The health needs of the state, community medicine, and the consideration of culture as well as social determinants of health are incorporated into the learning framework throughout all four years of medical school.  Medical students are exposed to patient care during their first year and engage in a 6-week in-depth clinical immersion experience during the pre-clinical years in a New Mexico community. The goals of the curriculum are to graduate physicians who are dedicated to providing excellent care to their patients, are enthusiastic about and responsible for their continued learning, and have a broad perspective on the role of physicians in the community.
medSchoolCurriculum.primaryCarePrograms: The UNM SOM has a strong commitment to primary care training for medical students. An important mission of the institution is to train future physicians to practice throughout the state of New Mexico. Medical students begin working with patients in their first year and most of these early clinical experiences are in primary care. Students spend 6 weeks in a community-based primary care practice during their pre-clinical years as a community and clinical immersion experience. The majority of students continue to work in their primary care continuity clinics, a longitudinal experience, throughout their second year. All students complete an 8-week Family Medicine clerkship during their 3rd year. The SOM offers residency programs in all primary care fields.  All of these programs provide required or elective experiences for residence in community settings.
medSchoolCurriculum.researchPrograms: Learning to think independently and scientifically when identifying and approaching medical problems are crucial skills that medical students must master. Each medical student at the UNM SOM is required to actively participate in solving a medical research problem with a research mentor. The scholarly project goal guides students to learn the process of applying the scientific method to solve health and medical problems, whether in the laboratory, clinic or community. The research requirements consists of two elements: 1) an experiential component where the student performs either a primary research, quality improvement project, or integrative review under the guidance of a qualified research mentor; and 2) a communication component where the student presents their research results in one of three ways: 1) oral or poster format, 2) paper, or 3) publication.
medSchoolCurriculum.communityServiceText: 10 hrs/wk during PIE. Students develop skills to engage community partners & stimulate personal, social, & intellectual growth. Service hours include those spent in service & in community learning.
medSchoolCurriculum.researchThesisText: A scholarly project and report is required.
medSchoolCurriculum.affiliatedHospitals: UNM Hospital, UNM Carrie Tingley Hospital, UNM Children's Hospital, UNM Children's Psychiatric Center, UNM Cancer Center, New Mexico VA Hospital, and UNM Sandoval Regional Medical Center.

medSchoolInformation.generalInformation: The University of New Mexico enrolled its first medical school class in 1964. The School of Medicine is both a professional and graduate school where students may earn an MD degree, a PhD degree, a Combined MD/PhD degree, a Combined MD/MPH degree, a Combined BA/MD degree, or BS and MS degrees in several allied health science fields. Medical education at the resident and postgraduate levels is offered through the University's teaching hospital and various state-of-the-art facilities. The University of New Mexico Hospital serves as the main teaching hospital, where we offer 24-hour translation services in Spanish, Navajo, and Vietnamese.
medSchoolInformation.missionStatement:
Our mission is to advance the health of all New Mexicans by educating and increasing the diversity of health professionals, leaders and scientists, providing outstanding and compassionate medical care, advocating for the health of all New Mexicans, and pursuing new knowledge, and excellence of practice.

Mission Impact in Admissions
• We observe mission-aligned selection practices when assessing applicants. Once minimum requirements have been met, we blind interviewers to the MCAT, GPA, and academic record of applicants. This allows us to select applicants who align with our mission and who are committed to improving healthcare in our local communities.
• We recognize the importance of rural and community physicians in addressing health equity issues. By involving them in our admissions committee they provide valuable perspectives to the selection process.
• In an effort to support applicants unsuccessful in gaining admissions, and/or from rural and underserved communities or low socioeconomic backgrounds, we provide a post application workshop, and individual consultations with specific recommendations to help individuals improve future applications. 

Mission Impact in Medical School Curriculum
• We provide students with the opportunity to engage in faculty-mentored scholarly projects related to health care issues in local communities. The focus on the Rural and Urban Underserved Program (RUUP) adds a significant dimension by allowing students to work directly with medically underserved communities. 
• The Practical Immersion Experience is a 6-week rural community-based clinical preceptorship, where students live in the assigned community. This provides a unique and immersive learning opportunity with first-hand experience to observe and understand daily life in a rural community, gaining insights into the specific community healthcare challenges and needs.
• Medical students participate in Learning Communities, which provide students with a support structure that includes a faculty mentor and upper classmates. This fosters a sense of community and mentorship, creating a supportive environment for students. 
• Incorporating Cultural Humility into our curriculum provides opportunities for students to learn about the populations they serve, such as teaching about use of birthing sashes in Navajo births and cleansing ceremony for local tribal and Native students. This approach enriches educational experience for students, and prepares them to provide culturally sensitive and patient-centered care.

Mission Impact in Medical School Student Support
• The HSC Center for Native American Health plays a pivotal role in addressing health-related needs and fostering collaboration within Native American Communities. Its specialization in various areas include; student and workforce development, community engagement, community-based participatory research, community health assessment capacity building, program planning, and project management.
• The Learning Environment Office mission is to foster an inclusive learning environment where teachers, staff, and learners thrive, and relationships are mutually respectful and beneficial to each other and to institutional climate. The initiatives, such as the speaker series, demonstrate a commitment to fostering respect, connection, and inclusion.

Mission Impact in Graduates
• 2025, UNM SOM ranked in Tier 1 for its Primary Care program in the US News and World Report. UNM SOM also ranked in Tier 3 for Research, and #23 for Most Graduates Practicing in Health Professional Shortage Areas
• Approximately 24% of all UNM-trained physicians are practicing in New Mexico
• UNM-trained physicians are practicing in 30 of New Mexico’s 33 counties
• 45% of all UNM-trained physicians practicing in New Mexico are in primary care specialties of Family Medicine, Internal Medicine, OB/GYN, or Pediatrics.
medSchoolInformation.programUndergradCollege: University of New Mexico College of Arts & Sciences
medSchoolInformation.programAbout: The Combined BA/MD Degree Program is a partnership program between the UNM College of Arts & Sciences and the UNM School of Medicine. The Program is designed to help address New Mexico’s physician shortage by assembling a class of diverse students who are committed to serving communities across the state. Students earn a baccalaureate degree through the College of Arts & Sciences in a challenging four-year curriculum specifically designed to prepare them for medical school. Upon successfully completing the undergraduate academic and eligibility requirements of the program, students will then transition to the School of Medicine to complete their MD degree.

medSchoolApplication.cbcRequired: A criminal background check is required for all accepted applicants
medSchoolApplication.applicantResponseToOffer: This is dependent upon when the offer of admissions offer is made to an applicant. Please contact our office at 505-272-4766 or somadmissions@salud.unm.edu for more information.
medSchoolApplication.amcasLettersText: All letters of recommendation must be received by Office of Admissions prior to the interview date and/or NO later than December 1st (whichever comes first). Any letters of recommendation received after the date of the interview or after December 1st will not be included in the application.
medSchoolApplication.letterGuidance:
It is suggested that applicants obtain letters from the following:

- One or more letter(s) from a clinician, such as a nurse or physician with whom you performed your clinical experience
- One or more letter(s) from a person with whom you worked on a project (research mentor, program director, commanding officer or work supervisor)
- One or more letter(s) from professors/faculty instructors*

*Applicants who have been away from degree-granting academic programs for several years may elect to submit letters from individuals other than professors.
medSchoolApplication.typicalInterviewDay:
Interviews are granted by invitation only. The interview provides the medical school with an opportunity to learn more about an applicant’s maturity, motivation for the study of medicine, problem-solving skills, ability to relate to people, and ability to express their ideas in an organized manner. Interviewers will be interested in determining how applicants meet our mission and might contribute to both the learning environment, and to the unique health care needs in New Mexico.

Interviews can last from 30 minutes to an hour, depending on the interviewer.
medSchoolApplication.interviewInvitations: The UNM School of Medicine typically begins sending interview invitations in mid-August.
medSchoolApplication.interviewFormat: Two one-on-one interviews conducted by Application Committee members.
medSchoolApplication.videoInterview: All interviews will  be conducted virtually via Zoom for the 2027 application cycle.
medSchoolApplication.secApplSentTo: The UNM SOM sends a Secondary Application to all individuals who submit a Primary AMCAS application. Applicants are responsible for ensuring they meet minimum requirements prior to submission.
medSchoolApplication.secApplLatestDtText: Once UNM SOM sends the Secondary Application to an an applicant, they are given 14 days to complete and submit.

medSchoolApplication.additionalInfo:
UNM SOM policy traditionally allows applicants to take up to two prerequisite lecture courses online. All labs must be completed in person. If an applicant exceeds the two online lecture prerequisite courses, or has taken labs online, they will have an opportunity to explain their circumstances for taking more than the allotted two lecture courses online through a formal prerequisite waiver process. The committee will review this information and it will be taken into consideration on a case-by-case basis.

Blended/Fusion Classes: 
UNM SOM considers any blended/fusion or hybrid classes as taken Online. If more than two lectures are taken online then applicants will have the opportunity to submit a prerequisite waiver explaining their circumstances. 

We are also aware of the disruptions the COVID-19 pandemic may have caused some current applicants in fulfilling the admissions requirements and have some exceptions to online course policy listed below:

Online Classes:
We will consider prerequisite lectures/labs that were converted to online during the Spring 2020 semester. Additionally, we will permit online lectures/labs taken through Spring 2023. Outside of the semesters listed above, no more than two prerequisite lectures may be taken online, and all labs must be completed in person. If more than two lectures are taken online, then applicants will have the opportunity to submit a prerequisite waiver explaining their circumstances. 

Credit/No Credit or Pass/Fail Grades:
Applicants that received Credit/No Credit or Pass/Fail grades in lieu of a letter grade for prerequisite courses during the Spring 2020 through Spring 2022 semesters/quarters, will have an opportunity to explain their circumstances for which the prerequisite courses are completed outside our guidelines. Outside of the semesters listed above all prerequisite coursework must receive a letter grade of a C or better (C- not acceptable).
medSchoolApplication.mcatScoresAdditionalInfo: We utilize a mission-aligned selection and retention approach when assessing the applicant's entire application, including the MCAT score. Once minimum requirements have been met, we blind interviewers to the MCAT, as well as the GPA and academic record of applicants. This allows us to select applicants who align with our mission and who are committed to improving healthcare in our local communities.
medSchoolApplication.mcatScreenAdditionalInfo: Applicants must receive a minimum composite MCAT score of a 494 to be considered for admissions.
medSchoolApplication.gpaScreenAdditionalInfo: Applicants must have a minimum cumulative weighted OR unweighted GPA of a 3.0 (including postbaccalaureate and/or graduate level coursework) to be considered for admissions.
medSchoolApplication.courseworkAcceptanceInfo: Prerequisite coursework may be taken at a community college as long as the courses completed meet our class and credit hour requirements. Please note: any accelerated or dual-credit coursework done during high school must be included, along with a letter grade, on official college transcripts. Please see https://hsc.unm.edu/medicine/education/md/admissions/apply/prerequisite-courses.html for more information.
medSchoolApplication.letterOfIntentAdditionalInfo:
Once an applicant has submitted the AMCAS application, they may only make the permitted changes listed here: https://students-residents.aamc.org/applying-medical-school-amcas/amcas-postsubmission-actions .

Applicants may provide verbal updates during their interviews, but once the interviews are completed they may not submit any letters of intent, or modifications to an application.
medSchoolApplication.technicalStandardInfo:
A candidate for the MD degree at the University of New Mexico School of Medicine (UNM SOM) must demonstrate the capacity to acquire the knowledge, attitudes, and skills necessary to complete the MD Program educational requirements, including the technical standards outlined below. Graduates will achieve the MD Program competencies in the basic and clinical sciences, and they will be able to graduate as skilled and eﬀective practitioners of medicine with or without reasonable accommodations. 

The abilities and characteristics which follow are deﬁned as technical standards, which, in conjunction with academic standards, are requirements for admission, promotion, and graduation. The medical curriculum requires demonstrated proﬁciency in a variety of skills. UNM SOM requires that each student be able to meet the following technical standards: Observation, Communication, Motor Coordination, Examination and Diagnostic Skills, Intellect, and Behavioral and Social Attributes.

medSchoolFinancial.financialAid:
The HSC Financial Aid Office makes accessible to all students information and application processes for federal (Title IV and VII), state and institutional aid programs. These resources include: scholarships, grants and loans. Institutional aid consists of both need and merit based scholarships. Award amounts vary upon qualified candidates and funding levels. The Financial Aid website provides information about financial aid funding opportunities and policies to incoming and current students. A financial literacy program is also offered to all students, beginning with the first year through fourth year. This program consists not only of one-on-one counseling, but group sessions on various topics, such as understanding credit and FICO scores.

Financial Aid website: https://hsc.unm.edu/academic-affairs/offices/financial-aid/

medSchoolPrograms.info:
The MD/PhD program is designed to provide comprehensive training in both clinical sciences and either Basic Biomedical Sciences, Healthy Equity Sciences, or Engineering. The intent of the program is to provide students with an integrated and cohesive training experience while obtaining the MD/PhD degree. Students participate in activities common to both programs while involved in the medical school curriculum or engaged in PhD dissertation research. The program consists of 2 years of the medical school curriculum followed by 3-4 years of graduate courses and PhD dissertation research, and concludes with the remaining 2 years of the medical school curriculum. The PhD and MD degrees are awarded simultaneously at the end of the entire training period. Students can pursue many lines of research activity performed by investigators in biomedical research in the School of Medicine.

Note: The UNM SOM now considers all non-resident applicants for the combined MD/PhD program only.

The following programs are designed to help undergraduate students prepare for their application to medical school:
- New Mexico Clinical Education Program (ClinEd): https://hsc.unm.edu/diversity/programs/community/clinical-education.html
- MCAT Test Prep Program: https://hsc.unm.edu/diversity/programs/community/test-prep.html
- Undergraduate Health Sciences Enrichment Program (UHSEP): https://hsc.unm.edu/diversity/programs/community/uhsep.html
- Undergraduate Student Scholars Program: https://hsc.unm.edu/diversity/programs/community/undergraduate-student-scholars-program.html

The Premedical Enrichment Program (PrEP) is a 2-semester post-baccalaureate program that facilitates entrance into medical school by offering curriculum to educationally disadvantaged students who exhibit exceptional non-cognitive characteristics but who aren't eligible for direct admission due to low MCAT or GPA. Learn more: https://hsc.unm.edu/diversity/programs/community/premed-enrichment-program.html.

medSchoolSelection.premedReqRec:
- All prerequisite coursework must be completed with a letter grade of C or better (C- is not acceptable) and must be taken in the United States at a college or university recognized by one of the U.S. Regional Accrediting Agencies. We will NOT permit prerequisite coursework taken outside of the U.S.
- Pass/Fail (CR/NC) grading is only acceptable from Spring 2020 through Spring 2022 (See "Admissions Policies & Information" for further detail)
- Advance Placement (AP) & International Baccalaureate Credit will be accepted for introductory Biology, Chemistry, or Physics ONLY if college credit was granted by the institution. 
- College Level Examination Program (CLEP) Credit will be accepted as long as the applicant has the sufficient number of semester hours to fulfill the required prerequisites
- Biology courses must be human-based. Non-human biology courses will NOT be accepted (e.g. Zoology, Plant Ecology, etc.)
medSchoolSelection.oldestPrereqDate: The UNM SOM does not have an expiration date for prerequisite coursework.
medSchoolSelection.selectionFactors:
In general, only those applicants with strong ties to the state of New Mexico, members of U.S. Federal Tribal Sovereign Nations, active duty military members stationed in New Mexico, and residents of WICHE states (Montana and Wyoming) will receive consideration for admissions. 

Strong ties include graduating from a New Mexico high school that was attended for at least one year, being 22 or younger and financially dependent on a New Mexico resident, holding a degree (at any level) from a New Mexico college or university, or being a legal resident or high school graduate of a U.S. county bordering New Mexico. Applicants may be asked to provide proof of residency at any point throughout the admissions cycle.

Additionally, selection is based upon many factors, including, but not limited to, academic achievement, performance on the MCAT, personal statement, secondary application, interviews, professionalism, clinical experience, community service, and letters of recommendation.
medSchoolSelection.preMedShadowText:
The Committee on Admissions carefully reviews each type of clinical experience in which every individual applicant to medical school has participated. The Committee believes that every applicant should reflect a vibrant interest in medicine demonstrated by clinical experiences with direct patient contact and knowledge of New Mexico's health care issues. The intent is to provide the applicant with the opportunity to prove to themselves and to the Committee on Admissions that medicine is the profession in which the individual whole-heartedly wishes to study and work. This volunteer or possible work experience may be in a hospital or clinical setting, or perhaps in a nursing home or hospice environment.

It is up to each student to take initiative to locate their clinical experiences through interactions with the various volunteer offices of the local hospitals or through interactions with their professors, friends, family members, etc.
